page: Amazon Web Services c7i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The CPU includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning and matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio.

Performance benchmarks show strong capabilities in specific workloads. The server achieves a top-tier rating in LLM text generation for small models (135M) at 380.26 tokens/sec, and strong performance in prompt processing for medium models (7B) at 206.92 tokens/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and static web serving throughput are also strong, reaching 32.2 GB/sec and 48.15 GB/sec respectively. Other metrics, including Geekbench multi-core (14186.0) and Redis SET operations (38.5 million operations/sec), fall into the average tier.

This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, meaning storage requirements must be met via network-attached options, utilizing the baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The lack of local storage and GPUs represents a tradeoff for workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space or hardware acceleration. However, the high-speed DDR5 memory and dedicated compute resources make it a cost-efficient choice for CPU-bound tasks, such as web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale machine learning inference.
